rationale: Evidence: Iteration 1 (score 289) is the best so far. Its oval finish rate was 0.65 with mean time 1.73 s, so speed is not the bottleneck on gentle curves. Every s-bend and slalom trial still left the track at progress 0.11 to 0.22, with max_error about 0.062 to 0.064, just above the 0.06 m off-track limit. Body width is already at its maximum, so that limit cannot be widened. Steering oscillation and RMS error are small, so the robot is not oscillating. It is being pushed outward on bends, which means it lacks steering authority or responsiveness. Iteration 2 changed sensor width, wheel_track, base_speed, and kp together. Its oval finish rate dropped to 0.45, while s-bend progress rose slightly (0.22 to 0.31). That suggests kp and turn-rate changes help sharp bends but that the sensor and speed changes did not. I therefore keep the iteration 1 sensor layout (12 mm footprints, x = -0.03 to +0.03, y = 0.05), which had the best oval result, and make a narrower change: wheel_track 0.12 to 0.10 for a faster turn per unit of turn command, kp 4 to 5 for more correction, kd 0.6 to 0.8 to damp it, and base_speed kept at 1.2 for oval finish time. ki stays at 0.2 for the motor mismatch and mass stays at 0.6 kg. Expected result: progress on s-bend and slalom rises above 0.3, with line_loss_events falling below 1. Oval completion should hold at or above 0.6. Hypotheses: (H1) the faster turn rate from the narrower wheel track is the main driver of better bend tracking; (H2) if steering_oscillation rises above about 0.5, kp is too high and should drop to 4.5. Measurements next: per-track completion, progress, max_error against the 0.06 limit, line_loss_events, and completion_time on the oval.
